a: A sub-step angle turns a glyph that cannot rotate on the painted tier but not on the baked one
cursorFor answers a cached cursor for an unknown glyph name instead of throwing
brushRing(-Infinity) does not throw, and draws at the default 24 px
bakeFallback accepts fallbacks that make the browser drop the whole declaration
A CursorSink cannot give the element back once setBase has been called
b: brushRing's Infinity guard misses a finite radius whose size overflows, which then draws at the default 24 px
An infinite `size` throws in bakeCursor/cursorFor but draws at 24 px through resolveCursor
A painted cursor's `fallback` is validated and then dropped, so with no painted layer the sink shows no cursor at all
On the painted tier, a glyph that cannot rotate is still turned by a small angle that the baked tier ignores
bakeFallback rejects only `;{}`, so any other value that is not a keyword still makes the browser drop the whole cursor silently
